Remarks: The water's sweet. Somebody did that with their own two hands.
First summer in years nobody's boiled the well water.
Conditions.Heard: They say Sill's well runs clear now. A stranger rebuilt the ring by hand.

Remarks: The Concord's man came round for the well money again.
Clean water, and a bill nailed by the door for it.
Conditions.Heard: Sill pays the Concord for its own water now, I hear.

Remarks: Bread every morning again. Smell that.
The oven's fine. The Concord's inspector says so, every season, for a fee.
The watch can see the bend in the road all night now.
Conditions.Heard: Sill keeps a proper light on its road again. Safer going that way.

Remarks: That sealed lantern of the Concord's never gutters. Nobody here knows how it works.
Perch in the nets again. The weir's holding.
The old men are down at the weir arguing about it again. Let them be.
Conditions.Heard: Tine's weir is mended, they say. There'll be perch on the boats this season.

Remarks: The Concord's weir works. So does the Concord's catch-tax.
The scribe finished her copy. She says the gap in it is the best part.
The scribe has a new margin in her copy. She read it to us twice.
Conditions.Heard: The old copyist at Tine has entered the third hand. Someone carried it to her.

Remarks: The registrar entered six crates. The drover's allowed to stand up now.
Conditions.Heard: Cloth caravans will go through Gantry again. Their registrar counted six.

Remarks: The exchange floor is smiling at everybody. Somebody signed something for them.
Conditions.Heard: Gantry signed a short count against a caravan of the cloth. Go through there with your crates where you can see them.

Remarks: There is shade under the cloth again. Sit.
Conditions.Heard: A stranger rehung the guest-cloth at Gantry. The oath keeps there.

Remarks: The guest bowl is full. Someone saw to it.
No more paying for a bridge nobody built.
Conditions.Heard: Sill's road-tithe has a new hand on the roll: no bridge, nothing owing. First hand that ever said no bridge.

Remarks: We've stopped paying the bridge money. Let them come and show us the bridge.
We paid the bridge money. There's still no bridge.
The east composition is finished. Walk to the well before you look at it.
Conditions.Heard: Posy finished its east composition, they say. People are walking a day to stand at their well and turn round.

Remarks: You were in the east composition. People still stand where you stood.
She keeps the evening you were held. She will not say where.
The copy-desks are lit through the evening again. Pages entered after dark.
The condition report on the First Account has its last line now.
Conditions.Heard: Quillhold's conservators finished the line on the First Account's report. The old copyist will want to hear.

Remarks: Tally sent for the farmer's seed money. She paid them in words, not drams.
Somebody paid the farmer's account at Tally. She keeps asking who.
The tenants of the disused wing are filed now. Classification: Catchers. Status: continuing.
Conditions.Heard: Marrowstye has filed its disused wing under Catchers. The central file has opened a drawer for them.

Remarks: Three intake cards voided by the central file. The subjects have their words back.
The east cut's being worked. Smell the racks.
Conditions.Heard: Sumphold's cutting the east bank again, I hear. Somebody saw off the bandfrogs.

Remarks: The Concord's pest man takes a share of every rack now.
The lamps are lit east of the well. You can see it at night. Nobody looks.
Somebody read the east wall aloud. All of it. I heard my mother's name and it was still hers.
Conditions.Heard: Someone stood at Slip's east wall and read out every name. In the dark, they say.

Remarks: Somebody walked out to the dry wash and faced Harl's kin where they camped. The guest never left the shade, and never had to.
Somebody not of our tents stood at the wash. We will not ask who. We will offer them water.
Conditions.Heard: From Wellmeet: Harl's kin were camped in the dry wash, waiting out a guest's three days. A stranger walked out and faced them there, away from the tents.

Remarks: Harl's kin took the price and went home. She owes them nothing now. The oath was never in it.
Conditions.Heard: Wellmeet settled a blood-debt in drams, they say. Forty-five. Tidy work, for the tents.

Remarks: There is a keeper from the First Tent at the pole. She hears both sides, and then the oath says its piece.
Conditions.Heard: Water was poured for the keeper who went down to Wellmeet before anyone asked her a single thing. A guest there sent her word to us, and it will be heard after the third day.

Remarks: The scales are true. The carters weigh in front of us now, and say nothing.
'Guest-right, valued.' Somebody read their tare-book out at the pans. The carters have not stopped apologising.
A tenth of every load, for the water we give. You may laugh. We have.
Conditions.Heard: Somebody read the Exchange's tare-book at Wellmeet. They had valued the tents' hospitality at a tenth of every load. The rate is under review.

Remarks: Filed under what she wrote. Cross-filed under what she may have said. Whether written governs said is pending.
'Then I'll not need the lamp.' Filed. You may visit her by it.
Conditions.Heard: Circular from the Vault: the Wellmeet road intake has been moved from unrecorded to her last words, on a witness's mark. Marrowstye is asked to note the precedent.

Remarks: Stake nine, checked at first light: in place. Stake eleven: in place. The sorter has stopped writing 'shifting'.
The eleventh's entry for the cut has it quiet after dark. It read 'claimed'. It now reads 'confirmed', in the same hand, smaller.
The new line follows the tenth's numbers. Where the tenth wrote nothing, at stake ten, the eleventh has left the space blank too, and initialled the blank.
Conditions.Heard: Word from the Drowned Ledger: the eleventh has set the bed by the tenth recension's survey, blank at stake ten and all, and sent us a fair copy. Ours shows a stake ten. One of the two has been wrong for a long while.

Remarks: Proper ward in the jars. Sit low; the light's good tonight.
The ward smells of upstairs. It'll do. It's doing.
The salt-carrier walked out of here under a stranger's cloth, with the clan watching from the poles. Not one of them stood up. That is the oath, and it was hard to watch.
Conditions.Heard: From the First Tent: a carrier went out under a second cloth when the first one ended, and her pursuers were the host's own clan. They sat. They kept it.

Remarks: The clan was paid for the salt and went home. The contract is settled. The cloth was never part of it, and nobody here pretends otherwise.
Conditions.Heard: Carriage dispute at the First Tent, settled in drams by a third party. Tent-Right accounts are rarely this tidy. We've noted the rate.

Remarks: Somebody read the first cord out loud at the poles, all of it, and the clan sat through it. The first host was hosting her own clan's enemy. They knew that. Hearing it said is a different thing.
Conditions.Heard: At the First Tent someone read the first cord out to a clan at the poles, and the clan went home.

Remarks: We've filed the first counter's last ledger with Tally as our reason, terms and all. Head office has gone quiet. That usually means they're pricing it.
Conditions.Heard: Revised rate for the far east route: the Last Counter has filed a reason, and the reason is on the account. Carriage beyond the point stays unguaranteed. The rate is under review.

Remarks: The road east was quiet this morning. Not safe. Quiet. We're selling that difference at a fair rate.
Continuity surcharge paid, by a customer, which is a first. It's on the prices now, naturally. Somebody has to carry it, and you're here.
Conditions.Heard: The Last Counter has been underwritten by a private party. The surcharge is being passed on at the counter, as is proper.

Remarks: You can hear the pump from the well, if you listen. Thump, and wait, and thump. Sounds like a slow heart, my gran would say. It isn't. It's a pump.
The lads go down the north field path again. They take a lamp and a spade and they don't sing, which is new.
Clay in the seep, and the level's drying. The spring in the grove's gone to a trickle, they say. Nobody here goes up there to look.
Conditions.Heard: The grove spring above Cinderhold has dropped to a trickle since they clayed the mine seep. The beetles have moved their path.
